MX17 at LNL · target options · 22 Oct 2026

Pierfrancesco’s 20 µm lithium on diamond is the right target, on a thin membrane rather than 1 mm: at LNL the heat is easy, a thick backing costs the leptons, and the open questions are hydrogen, adhesion and vacuum.

A thermal model of every backing, nuclear yields from measured data for what the film and backing emit, and Geant4 (run L9) of the leptons through the target assembly.

1

Details

Pierfrancesco's reply to the LNL slides: the target is the critical issue. No fluorine; heat; the backing's background and the best backing; a cold trap for carbon; PIGE monitoring; the 441 keV γ and the window; the strip/clamp design; and his proposal of 20 µm Li on 1 mm diamond with micro-channel cooling. Each slide answers one of these. Write-up: lnl/target/TARGET_OPTIONS.md; the earlier fluorine/heat study is the note lnl-lithium-target.

For LNL: 20 µm Li on 8 µm Mo on a thin CVD diamond membrane, ring-cooled, in a cold shroud

Every element answers one of Pierfrancesco’s points. Hover the layers.

his pointanswer here
no fluorine; a lot of heatmetallic Li (×2.2 Li per keV of beam) on 50 µm diamond: 35 °C at 4 µA, < 150 °C to 30–40 µA
background from the backingMo/Ta stops the beam: no backing line above 1 MeV; bare diamond: 2.37 and 8.06 MeV, below the window
1 mm diamond, micro-channelsnot needed below ~30 µA, and ×1.4–1.9 slower per µA: legs cross it edge-on (Geant4 L9)
carbon; cold trapone LN₂ shroud pumps carbon and water (Li is a getter)
PIGE; germanium?478 keV to 1 % in 10–60 s; Ge only for the Na/B lines, and safe: no neutrons below 1.88 MeV

2

Details

Mo (or Ta) between the Li and the diamond does three jobs: it stops the 0.87 MeV protons (range 6 µm), so the hydrogen lands in a metal that tolerates ≥ 3.4×10¹⁹ /cm²; it carries the beam current away (diamond is an insulator); and it gives lithium something to wet, which an untreated diamond surface may not. The diamond's only job is to carry the heat.

A 20 µm lithium film gives ×8.2 the ⁸Be rate per proton and stays clear of the 441 keV resonance

Statistics were never LNL’s limit (1 d to 3σ at 1 µA). The gain buys a lower current: the same X17 rate at ~0.12 µA, with ×8 less heat, hydrogen and carbon. 15–25 µm keeps the 441 share below 1 %.

3

Details

opt_backing.py + target_model.layered_yield → stacks.csv. The X17 is normalised per total γ₀ as in FEAS (ATOMKI 2022 reported the anomaly in direct capture too). If it came from the M1 resonance only, the 20 µm gain is ×6.7. The 3D fit absorbs a known energy profile; a 20 % 441 share biases it by < 0.06 R_ATOMKI (TARGET_STUDY §8), so 0.85 % is negligible.

Diamond makes the heat a non-problem: below 30 °C at LNL’s 4 µA, below 150 °C up to a few hundred µA

4

Details

opt_thermal.py. Checks: a conduction-only disk agrees with the analytic Gaussian-source result to 0.7 %; the 10 µm Al disk of the earlier study gives 97.6 °C against 95 °C. Contacts: dry clamp 5×10³–10⁴ W/m²/K, braze 2×10⁵, water 2×10⁴, micro-channels as h_eff = 3×10⁴ (laminar, 200 × 300 µm channels at 400 µm pitch, 1 L/min, Δp 1.2 bar). Limits: Li film 150 °C, Li₂O 300 °C. LNL beam power is 1.1 W/µA: the issue on a thin foil is the conduction path, not the power.

Why the slide-7 clamp failed: 20 µm of Li conducts k·t = 1.7 mW/K sideways, 1 mm of diamond 1.8 W/K. The backing must be the conductor.

Above ~30 µA the contacts set the temperature, not the diamond: braze the rim, metallise the face

1 mm diamond, 20 µm Li, 100 µA: vary the rim-clamp contact and the Li/diamond interface

rim clamp to the cooled ring

Li/diamond interface

A dry clamp in vacuum (10³–10⁴) is the bottleneck: braze or indium. CVD-diamond gyrotron windows are brazed to Cu cuffs and edge-cooled the same way.

Nobody seems to have measured evaporated Li on diamond. A Ta/Mo/Ti layer (carbide-forming) is the standard fix, and the same layer stops the beam: one bench test answers it.

Diamond grade: k = 1000 instead of 1800 adds ~20 K at 100 µA. Irrelevant at LNL.

6

Details

Inputs: ⁷Li(p,p′γ) from Bykov et al. ARI 175 (2021) (thick Li 4.9×10⁶ /µC at 1.0 MeV); ¹³C(p,γ) 556 keV resonance from Skowronski et al. PRC 111 064611 (2025); ¹²C(p,γ) 457 keV resonance (ωγ 0.6 eV); ²⁷Al(p,γ) 632/773/992 keV (ωγ 0.26/0.13/1.91 eV, the first two ESTIMATE) and (p,p′)843 keV (2 mb, ESTIMATE ×3). Resonances are integrated analytically per energy step (checked against (λ²/2)ωγ/ε). Ta/Cu Coulomb excitation (≤ 1.1 MeV) not computed. No neutrons below E_p = 1.88 MeV.

Detector response: Geant4 L9 gam_7Li_bklines, 10⁷ γ in nine lines from the spot, big plastics; a leg = SiPM bar AND plastic ≥ 0.5 MIP. opt_rates.py → line_response.csv, rates_options.csv.

Details

X₀ only matters for a backing in the leptons’ path, i.e. a target at the centre; at +12 cm (Geant4 L9) the backing is behind the leptons.

Spec: H₂O ≤ 10⁻⁸ mbar at the target: LN₂ shroud + bake. Li₂O hydrates too.

Carbon, 14 days at 1 µA with no trap: γ₀ ×0.85 on the 20 µm Li, 441 share 2.3%; with a cold shield ×1.00. Carbon is a 441 keV-calibration problem, not a 1 MeV one.

8

Details

Hydrogen: Budker INP in-situ blistering under 2 MeV protons (Cu from 10¹⁹ /cm², dense at 3×10¹⁹; Ta unchanged at 3.4×10¹⁹, ≥ 6.7×10²⁰ claimed); diamond: 1.2×10¹⁷ /cm² at 350 keV blistered only after a > 1400 °C anneal, no MeV/room-temperature data found. Water/O₂: Hertz–Knudsen flux × sticking ≈ 1 on fresh Li (ESTIMATE ×3); the products stay on the target and dilute it. Carbon: ~1 C retained per proton without a trap (Peterson & Laubert 1977), ×10 less with a cold shield, none seen with a LN₂ trap at 10⁻⁷ mbar (Redigolo 2024). opt_backing.py, opt_monitor.py.

Geant4: keep the backing thin where the leptons cross it; for ⁸Be no offset moves a thick one out of the way

Geant4 L9, 2026-10-22 · relative comparison; the full template refit for the chosen design is a follow-up

9

Details

Geant4 L9 (MX17_Full_Geant branch lnl_target, multi-layer backings): per configuration 5×10⁵ X17 (m 16.8), 5×10⁵ M1 and 5×10⁵ E1 Born IPC at 18.15 MeV, 2×10⁷ ⁸Be γ (EPC). Big plastics, LNL-calibrated calorimetry, MM 15° + TOF, the opening angle and pointing about the target position. Reach: Asimov/Fisher fit in θ × |y| × n_down with M1, E1, γ₁ and EPC norms free, cosmics fixed, best E_sum window; scaled so the baseline equals the reference 3D fit (FEAS §14, 1.0 d at 1 µA). γ₁ uses the baseline L2 templates for every configuration. Per µA: the 20 µm Li films make ×8.2 the γ₀, so their days per µA include that gain; "µA for the baseline rate" is the current that gives the baseline's X17 rate.

10

Details

Full-energy efficiency at 478 keV, 10 cm: 60 % HPGe 4×10⁻³, 3″×3″ LaBr₃ 6×10⁻³ (±30 %), scaled as 1/d². Total rate ~4× the peak (ESTIMATE). Sensitivity: 10 % less Li → −7 to −9 % in the 478 yield; 10 µg/cm² carbon → −0.6 %. Window: XCOM μ/ρ(Al) 0.0838 (0.478 MeV), 0.0227 cm²/g (17.6 MeV); pair conversion (7/9) t/X₀; Highland at 8.6 MeV. opt_monitor.py.

Details

lxplus/g4tendl_check.py → g4tendl_check.csv.

gaps to close, and questions for Pierfrancesco and Stephan

Bench / beam tests that close the gaps

1. ~1 MeV protons on bare and Mo/Ta-coated CVD diamond to 10¹⁹–10²⁰ /cm²: blisters? graphitisation?

2. 20 µm Li on Mo/Ta-coated diamond: adhesion and interface thermal resistance.

3. A Li target at known water pressure, followed by PIGE + elastic p.

4. Clamp or braze a 50–100 µm diamond membrane to a cooled Cu ring; thermal-cycle it.

5. Simulation: the full 3D template refit for the chosen design; the real holder and LNL beam line in Geant4.

Questions

1. Li evaporated in situ, or moved under vacuum? Is there a Li evaporator at LNL?

2. Can the LNL target lab coat a CVD diamond membrane with 8 µm Mo/Ta and mount it? Diamond supplier?

3. A LN₂ shroud in the chamber; typical water partial pressure?

4. A HPGe at 0.5–1 m during the run?

5. Beam time on AN2000/CN for the diamond test before the run?
